Policy

Certification and independence policy

A programme can map to a curriculum without being accredited, and a credential can exist without being equivalent to another. This page says precisely what we claim and what we do not.

Our independence policy

  • Intellica owns its curriculum, teaching, practice items, labs, credential names, rules and decisions. Public curricula, standards and exam blueprints are references and mappings only.
  • Intellica is independent of iSAQB, arc42, ISO, IEC, IEEE, the Software Engineering Institute and every certification body. Nothing here suggests an affiliation, approval or partnership.
  • Intellica is not an accredited iSAQB training provider. We do not use iSAQB logos or seals, and we never say a learner is “iSAQB certified” because of an Intellica course.
  • We use no protected exam questions, leaked questions or confidential task briefs. Practice items are original and are not real exam questions.
  • A mapping shows which of our lessons relate to a published learning goal. It does not mean a course replaces, counts towards or predicts the result of any external exam, and it does not satisfy any experience requirement.
  • No Intellica credential has been issued yet. Course certificates show that you finished a course by its published rule and are self-reported. When a credential scheme launches, its handbook, rules, appeals process and renewal policy will be published first.

The six planned credentials

Working titles. None has been issued.

LevelWorking credential titleCapstone evidence
Level 1Intellica Foundation Architecture Certificate (working title)One architecture file for a system you know, built across all 14 lessons, and a mock-exam readiness report.
Level 2Intellica Architecture Documentation Professional (working title)A complete arc42 document for one system, with its decisions and risks recorded.
Level 3Intellica Architecture Design and Evaluation Professional (working title)One quality and decisions record built on top of your arc42 document.
Level 4Intellica Agentic Architecture Specialist (working title)One agent system design: tools as contracts, memory, limits, human approval, rules an agent must follow with the checks that enforce them, and an evaluation plan.
Level 5Intellica Architecture Governance Professional (working title)One governance pack: principles, checks, migration plan, dependency exits and compliance evidence.
Level 6Intellica Lead Architect (working title)An architecture strategy document, presented and defended against hard questions.

How a level will be earned

Knowledge is necessary, not sufficient

Each open course combines quiz questions with a lab that builds a real artefact. Higher levels will add reviewed design work and an oral defence, because recognising terms is not the same as designing.

Evidence you can inspect

Every lesson ends in a lab section that adds to one record, so what you built is on the page, not only a score.

Checks that tell the truth

Health checks look for completeness, not for a good design. The pages say so, and rubrics in each lesson show what missing, partial and competent work looks like.

Practice that is separate from assessment

Mock exams are practice. A learner can take a paper again; the readiness report says what is weak. They do not predict an external result.

Separated decisions

When a credential scheme exists, the people who teach a level will not decide whether a candidate meets its standard, and appeals will go to someone who did not assess the candidate.

Design benchmark, not a claim

ISO/IEC 17024:2026 guides how a person-certification scheme should be designed. Intellica makes no accreditation or conformity claim.

Reading the market precisely

Different things get called accreditation. We keep them apart.

KindWhat it meansHow we use it
Professional certificationA body certifies that an individual met its own exam, experience and renewal requirements.Map public topics. Never claim equivalence or award another body’s credential.
Accredited training providerA body such as iSAQB accredits a provider and its course against its rules.Intellica is not one, and says so.
Accredited personnel certificationAn independent accreditation body assesses a certification body against a standard such as ISO/IEC 17024.A long-term design benchmark for our own scheme. We make no accreditation claim.
Framework or templateA structure such as arc42, or a quality model such as ISO/IEC 25010.Source material and vocabulary. It is not a personal certification.
Course alignmentA provider maps lessons to public topics.We publish the mapping with the disclaimer above.

What you get today

Each live course issues a completion certificate when you meet its published rule: finish every lesson and lab step, pass its health checks and answer at least 70 percent of the check questions correctly. It is a record based on your own reported progress, not an Intellica academy credential and not an iSAQB certificate. See the course pages for exactly what it attests.

Reviewed 2026-11-25. Intellica is independent of iSAQB, arc42, ISO, IEC, IEEE and the Software Engineering Institute. Mappings show how our lessons relate to published topics. They are not an affiliation, an approval or a prediction of any exam result.
